transcript.text: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. As we approach the production launch of the new event-ingestion service next Monday, I want to make sure we're all aligned. Before I record the final design, I need to go through our routine sign-off checklist. I'd like to hear from backend engineering, infrastructure, customer success operations, and security — any blockers or required controls from your side? Let's start with whoever's ready.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I have a blocker to raise. While reviewing an unrelated consumer integration this morning, I confirmed that the existing Ledger event consumer cannot preserve ordering across active-active replication. Production compatibility requires active-passive replication plus an explicit per-aggregate ordering guardrail. I have not yet updated the architecture document, so the draft design's active-active replication proposal is incompatible with our current production consumers.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a capacity blocker to raise. I confirmed from the current production load model just ten minutes ago that the shared cluster can support at most 48 partitions for this service without starving the checkout stream — not the 96 partitions in the draft design. I was still reconciling the capacity worksheet and hadn't posted the number yet, but this needs to be factored in before we finalize.

transcript.text: I have a blocker from customer success operations. In a contract review this afternoon, I found that our enterprise tenant Linden requires all event processing and storage to remain in the EU region. Linden is included in the proposed initial cohort, and I have not yet added the required EU-only routing exception to the design ticket. The current draft design does not account for this data-residency requirement.

transcript.text: I have a security blocker to raise. During a separate token-hardening task today, my security scan found personal data in the event payloads. This means the service requires field-level encryption and a maximum 30-day retention period — the draft design's 90-day retention period is insufficient. I have not yet opened the security finding, but these controls must be factored in before we finalize.
